values.title: A Woodland Habitat
values.text: Notice the layers of a living landscape.

A woodland is a living neighborhood. Trees form a canopy, shrubs provide shelter, and the forest floor supports fungi, insects, and new growth. Use this page as a field notebook: add observations, photographs, and questions as you explore.

values.alt: An illustrated woodland with layered trees and a winding path
values.caption: Look for the layers: canopy, understory, and forest floor.

values.title: Try a five-minute survey
values.text: Choose one small patch. Record three textures, two sounds, and one sign of animal life. Return later and notice what has changed.

## A closer look

Record the **canopy**, the *understory*, and the forest floor as separate habitats.

- Sketch one leaf shape.
- Look for tracks without disturbing wildlife.
- Add a question for your next visit.

values.caption: Different views of the same living landscape.
